column3: Frames believers' condition as steadfastness beyond weakness and grief.
Shows Satan attaching to one who slips away from received signs.
Presents fear for the vulnerable as prompting God-conscious, upright response.
Pairs fear of opponents with crossing the threshold, trust in God, and belief.
The immediate prior threat report becomes increased faith and reliance on God.
Uses fear within a distinct household-conflict setting.
Names Satanic secret counsel as grief-making, bounded by God, with reliance directed to God.
Locates demonic descent among particular recipients, extending the Satanic-agent side.
Shows Satan inciting then disavowing; its stated God-fear is contrary boundary evidence.
Defines God's allies by the absence of fear and grief.
Completes the immediate scene with protected return and pursuit of God's approval.
Distinguishes divine warning through signs from the fear manufactured in the focus.
Offers a general belief-conditioned warning against recurrence, without the fear relation.
Further identifies the recipients of demonic descent, largely repeating the prior card.
Presents divine warning as calling servants toward God-consciousness.
Explicitly identifies Satan as an enemy whose call gathers a doomed party.
Opens the question of alleged patronage and worship behind the focus's allies.
Presents a messenger's protective fear for his people, a different fear orientation.
Warns believers against taking hostile mockers as allies and directs fear to God.
Rejects claimed patronage and relocates worship toward jinn, clarifying false allegiance.
Links piety and reform to freedom from fear and grief, though redundant with 10:62.
General worship and reform instruction adds little to the focus's fear relation.
Supplies faith and God-consciousness as the qualities of the fear-free allies.
Shows fear as watchfulness in a personal danger scene, without the focus's redirection.
Connects fear of punishment with becoming Satan's ally, directly joining both focus poles.
Its faith-and-good-action promise is only a remote protective parallel.
Separates reassurance against fear and grief in a rescue scene.
Distinguishes claimed guardians from the God-conscious rightful guardians.
Makes seeking God's refuge from Satan a concrete protective response.
Sets belief and good action alongside no fear or grief, but repeats that outcome.
General call to worship and God-consciousness offers little specific help.
Satanic agents under guard do not clarify the focus's fear or allegiance relation.
Uses fear as a protective historical warning for a community.
In the same battle setting, attributes withdrawal to Satan while retaining divine pardon.
Hidden belief and cautious argument form only an indirect parallel.
Treats a remaining sign as perceptible to those who fear punishment.
Marriage regulation does not add to the focus's relation.
Shows Satanic insertion being removed while God's signs are made firm.
Keeps a concrete fear calculation visible before later divine support.
Addresses material fear when a sacred boundary is enforced, with provision attributed to God.
Warns against Satan's steps toward indecency and marks divine grace as purifying.
Records a messenger's fear of rejection, a distinct human fear rather than commanded fear.
Explicitly redirects fear away from people and toward God.
Supplies the outcome of the Satanic incitement already shown in 59:16.
Gives a localized reassurance after escape from wrongdoing.
Identifies certain practices as Satanic work and commands separation from them.
Adds glad tidings for God's allies, extending the fear-free condition already established.
Shows fear of God restraining retaliatory violence.
Depicts Satan's call as lacking coercive authority and ending in disavowal.
Names Satanic provocation in a reconciliation account, but fear is absent.
Shows fearful flight and appeal for rescue in a personal danger scene.
Legal treatment of migrating women does not illuminate the focus.
Its imagery does not clarify fear, Satan, or allegiance in the focus.
The terse divine-taking formulation offers no clear additional route.
Debt documentation is unrelated to the focus.
A bare future satisfaction statement supplies no usable link.
Places fear of God within accountability for disobedience.
Again names Satan as a manifest enemy who can turn people aside.
Reiterates the no-fear/no-grief outcome without the patronage contrast.
Makes fear of betrayal lead to an open, principled response rather than paralysis.
A further prophetic warning is largely redundant with earlier warning cards.
General faith and God-consciousness language is only indirectly related.
Shows belief persisting under fear of a powerful persecuting authority.
Directly contests misplaced fear and ties security to the proper object of fear.
Pairs maternal fear with divine reassurance and a future promise.
Warns of Satanic deception, hidden observation, and Satanic allies.
Keeps fear as an inward response that need not determine subsequent action.
General summons to belief under covenant adds little beyond the focus's final condition.
Shows a fear response reversed by explicit reassurance and glad news.
Directly regulates taking allies and retains God-directed wariness as the governing boundary.
Joins fear of return to God with the absence of any other patron.
Forbids following Satan's steps while calling believers to enter wholly into peace.
A repeated prophetic fear-for-community formulation adds little after similar cards.
Its general faith condition and denial of guardianship are too indirect.
Shows fear of a coming day sustaining devotion amid worldly distractions.
Explicitly asks whether opponents are feared and declares God more deserving of fear.
Transforms flight from a frightening sign into return under divine reassurance.
Food instruction and belief language do not add a focused connection.
Portrays fear of the Lord as accompanying present devoted action.
General God-consciousness instruction is redundant and lacks the fear relation.
Explicitly contrasts others' fearmaking with God's sufficiency for the servant.
Identifies Satanic aims as enmity, hatred, and diversion from remembrance and prayer.
Makes lack of fear for the hereafter a diagnostic contrary to responsive warning.
Shows Satan's false assurance and later withdrawal, closely paralleling 59:16 in a conflict scene.
Balances fear and hope in invocation, offering a different disciplined fear orientation.
Recalls a hostile threat restrained by God and pairs God-consciousness with reliance.
Fear and hope occur together in a natural sign, a remote parallel.
Opposes fighting under God to fighting under false power and calls Satan's allies weak.
Reiterates the fear-and-hope natural sign with little new for the focus.
Links Satanic prompting to allies and warns that obedience reshapes allegiance.
Fear of exposure is a contrary, self-protective case rather than the commanded fear.
Covenant-breaking imagery does not clarify the focus.
The question about false associates only distantly echoes false allegiance.
Family-maintenance regulation is unrelated to the focus.
Resurrection argument supplies no specific fear, Satan, or allegiance relation.
Speech distortion and disobedience are too indirect for the focus.
The oath fragment provides no usable connection.
A battle narrative of later withdrawal offers only a distant contrary parallel.
The later separation of believers and hypocrites gives an eschatological allegiance boundary.
The isolated oath object adds no interpretable connection.
Links following divine guidance with freedom from fear and grief.
Connects wholehearted surrender and good action with no fear or grief.
Adds a charitable-action instance of no fear and grief, now highly redundant.
Repeats the no-fear/no-grief outcome for charitable action.
Again connects faith and righteous action with no fear or grief.
Makes divine support decisive against human opposition and directs reliance to God.
The immediate battle context shows believers responding after injury with God-consciousness.
Immediately follows the focus by forbidding grief over those hastening into disbelief.
Explicitly contrasts fear of people with fear due to God.
Treats hostile opposition as a concrete fear condition requiring guarded practice.
Names Satan as rebellious within the false-devotion field.
Presents Satan's declared program of taking a fixed share from people.
Extends Satan's program as misleading, wish-making, and command.
Contrasts Satan's promises and wish-making with their deception.
Explicitly commands fear away from opponents and toward God.
Explicitly prohibits fear of people and commands fear of God.
Shows fear of reversal shaping unreliable allegiance.
Counters fear of people with divine protection of the messenger.
Adds the recurring guidance, reform, no-fear/no-grief pattern.
Places devils among humans and jinn in reciprocal deceptive prompting.
Adds the no-fear/no-grief outcome in a recompense setting.
Shows God-conscious people recognizing and recovering after Satanic touch.
Provides the contrary continuation: Satanic fellows keep extending error.
Defines believers by hearts stirred at God's mention and growing trust.
Presents divine reassurance as stabilizing believers' hearts in conflict.
Recalls believers' former fear and vulnerability before divine shelter and aid.
Restricts fear in sacred stewardship to God.
Counters grief in danger with the declaration of divine presence.
Combines trust in God with refusal to be governed by contingent harm.
Directs believers under Pharaoh's threat to place trust in God.
Makes reliance on God the response to being made a trial by wrongdoers.
Names God as the best guardian and most merciful protector.
Affirms reliance on God while acknowledging that planning cannot override divine decree.
Joins fear of God with fear of an evil reckoning.
Makes reliance on God the shared stance of believers.
Denies Satan authority over God's devoted servants.
Records Satan's intention to entice broadly, setting the adversarial backdrop.
Shows fear of the Lord above as an obedient orientation.
Denies Satan authority over those who believe and rely on their Lord.
Locates Satan's authority among those who take him as patron and associate others.
Contrasts hoped mercy and feared punishment in relation to the one God.
Again denies Satan authority over God's servants.
Directly censures taking Satan and his offspring as protectors besides God.
Names fear of oppressive excess, then receives divine assurance of presence.
Answers fear with divine reassurance of superiority.
Links fear of the unseen Lord with receiving remembrance.
Places hope and fear together within responsive devotion.
Returns to the no-fear theme at the greatest terror.
Makes fear of God responsive to the gravity of the final Hour.
Characterizes believers by fear of their Lord.
Joins obedience with fear of God and God-consciousness.
Promises replacement of fear with security for faithful worshippers.
Shows Moses' earlier flight as a fear response before divine commissioning.
Exempts messengers from fear in the divine presence, subject to wrongdoing.
Records fear of being seized away as a pressure against guidance.
Shows hardship testing a claimed faith, a distant pressure parallel.
Connects patient action and reliance on God.
Places hope and fear together in devoted turning to God.
Commands reliance on God as sufficient guardian.
Shows fear overwhelming a community under siege, a contrary stress case.
Shows danger increasing believers in faith and surrender rather than fear-led retreat.
Explicitly contrasts fearing people with God being more deserving of fear.
Describes messengers fearing none but God.
Denies Satan independent authority, limiting his role to exposure of allegiance.
Links warning with those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer.
Places fear of God among those with knowledge.
Joins unseen fear of the Merciful with following remembrance.
Pairs avoidance of false powers with turning to God and glad tidings.
Presents bodily fear at God's discourse followed by softening toward His remembrance.
Gives believers the direct assurance not to fear or grieve.
Makes seeking refuge in God the response to a Satanic provocation.
Shows turning from remembrance resulting in a Satanic companion.
Contrasts worldly friendship with God-conscious friendship at final judgment.
Links steadfast confession of God with no fear and no grief.
Shows divine tranquility increasing faith under pressure.
Pairs unseen fear of the Merciful with a returning heart.
Recalls fear among one's people as part of a later saved condition.
Promises a distinct outcome to one who fears standing before the Lord.
Commands believers to fear God while preparing for what lies ahead.
Makes God the sole object of trust for believers.
Commands fearing God to one's capacity and responsive obedience.
Associates God-consciousness with an opening way out.
Completes that assurance with provision and reliance on God.
Commands believers to protect themselves and their families from the Fire.
Promises forgiveness and reward to those fearing their Lord unseen.
Describes the faithful as fearful of their Lord's punishment.
Makes God uniquely worthy of fear and forgiveness.
Links fear of standing before the Lord with restraining the self.
Places God's pleasure and the servant's pleasure with fear of the Lord.
